nodes.summary: The atoms of a proposition $A$ form the finite set of atoms occurring in $A$: an atom $x$ has the single atom $x$, and the atoms of $B \wedge C$, $B \vee C$ and $B \to C$ are the atoms of $B$ together with the atoms of $C$.
nodes.title: Atoms of a proposition

nodes.summary: For an atom $p$ and a proposition $A$, the Boolean quantification $\exists p.\, A$ is the disjunction $A[p := \top] \vee A[p := \bot]$, where $A[p := \top]$ and $A[p := \bot]$ replace the atom $p$ in $A$ by the constant $\top = (\bot \to \bot)$ and by $\bot$ respectively.
nodes.title: Boolean quantification over an atom

nodes.summary: For a list of atoms $p_1, \dots, p_n$ and a proposition $A$, the iterated Boolean quantification $\exists p_1 \cdots p_n.\, A$ is $\exists p_1.\, \exists p_2.\, \cdots \exists p_n.\, A$: $A$ is quantified over $p_n$ first and over $p_1$ last, and for the empty list the result is $A$ itself.
nodes.title: Boolean quantification over a list of atoms

nodes.summary: If two Boolean valuations $v$ and $w$ agree on every atom of a proposition $A$, then $A$ has the same truth-table value under $v$ as under $w$.
nodes.title: The truth value depends only on the atoms

nodes.summary: Let $p_1, \dots, p_n$ be a list of atoms that does not contain $\bot$, let $A$ be a proposition and let $v$ be a Boolean valuation with $v(\bot)$ false. Then the iterated Boolean quantification $\exists p_1 \cdots p_n.\, A$ is true under $v$ if and only if $A$ is true under some valuation $w$ that agrees with $v$ on every atom not in the list.
nodes.title: Truth of a Boolean quantification over a list of atoms

nodes.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be propositions such that $A \to B$ is derivable without assumptions in classical propositional logic $\mathrm{CPL}$ (natural deduction with the axioms $\neg\neg C \to C$). Then there is a proposition $I$ whose atoms all lie among the atoms common to $A$ and $B$ together with $\bot$, such that $A \to I$ and $I \to B$ are both derivable without assumptions in $\mathrm{CPL}$.
nodes.title: Craig interpolation for classical natural deduction

nodes.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be propositions such that every Boolean valuation $v$ with $v(\bot)$ false that makes $A$ true also makes $B$ true. Then there is a proposition $I$ whose atoms all lie among the atoms common to $A$ and $B$ together with $\bot$, such that every valuation $v$ with $v(\bot)$ false that makes $A$ true makes $I$ true, and every valuation $v$ with $v(\bot)$ false that makes $I$ true makes $B$ true.
nodes.title: Craig interpolation, semantic form

nodes.summary: For an atom $p$, a Boolean $b$ and a proposition $A$, the proposition $A[p := b]$ is obtained from $A$ by replacing every occurrence of the atom $p$ by the constant $\top$, written $\bot \to \bot$, if $b$ is true, and by $\bot$ if $b$ is false.
nodes.title: Substituting a truth value for an atom

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
